req.title: Create form GET returns 200
req.statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-038 requires GET /create to return HTTP 200 for authenticated users. Three test cases are needed: (1) positive — authenticated user receives 200 and the create form HTML; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected (302) not served the form; (3) boundary — the state transition from unauthenticated to authenticated (login boundary) then immediately hitting GET /create to confirm the exact 200. Each test uses exact status code assertions to kill comparison-operator mutations (== vs >=, 200 vs 302), checks response body content to kill constant mutations, and verifies the redirect location on the negative path to kill negation mutations.

tests.name: test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Rahul (id=1, password=stone) exists in the pre-loaded dataset
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
expected: Response body contains the create form indicator b'Create'
trace: R-FLASKR-038: authenticated GET /create must return HTTP 2xx (exactly 200)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_resp = client.post('/auth/login',
                             data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    resp = client.get('/create')
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert b'Create' in resp.data

test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200()

preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
No user is logged in (no session cookie)
expected: Response status code is exactly 302 (redirect), NOT 200

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_unauthenticated_returns_302_not_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    resp = client.get('/create')
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert resp.status_code != 200
    location = resp.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert location == '/auth/login'

test_create_get_unauthenticated_returns_302_not_200()

tests.name: test_create_get_exactly_at_auth_boundary_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Anjali (id=2, password=cloud) exists in the pre-loaded dataset
State: user transitions from unauthenticated to authenticated in the same client session
actions: Confirm GET /create before login returns 302 (unauthenticated state)
POST /auth/login with username=Anjali, password=cloud to cross the auth boundary
Immediately GET /create in the same session (authenticated state)
Assert status code is exactly 200 at the boundary crossing
expected: Login POST returns exactly 302 (redirect to index)
Response body contains b'Create' confirming the form is served
trace: R-FLASKR-038: state transition from unauthenticated (302) to authenticated (200) at GET /create boundary

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_exactly_at_auth_boundary_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    pre_resp = client.get('/create')
    assert pre_resp.status_code == 302
    assert pre_resp.status_code != 200
    login_resp = client.post('/auth/login',
                             data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert login_resp.status_code == 302
    post_resp = client.get('/create')
    assert post_resp.status_code == 200
    assert post_resp.status_code != 302
    assert b'Create' in post_resp.data

test_create_get_exactly_at_auth_boundary_returns_200()
